note: Reusable, representative task bank for benchmarking any model/provider added to the system. Re-run this same bank whenever a new model shows up (Codex, a new OpenCode Go model, etc.) so results stay comparable over time - not ad hoc one-offs. Each task targets a specific tier so a model's actual ceiling shows up as 'passes D/C, fails B/A', not a vague vibe.

tasks.prompt: Write a Python function is_palindrome(s) that checks if a string is a palindrome, ignoring case, spaces, and punctuation. Docstring + one example. Just code.
tasks.pass_criteria: Correct logic, handles case/spaces/punctuation, no crash on edge input.

tasks.prompt: Convert this into a proper docstring-documented function with type hints: def add(a,b): return a+b
tasks.pass_criteria: Adds type hints and a correct docstring without changing behavior.

tasks.prompt: Write a Python function merge_intervals(intervals) that merges overlapping intervals (list of [start,end] pairs), handles unsorted input, empty list, and touching intervals like [1,2],[2,3]. Include a docstring. Just the code.
tasks.pass_criteria: Sorts first, correctly merges touching intervals (<=, not <), handles empty list without crashing.

tasks.prompt: Write a README section documenting a REST endpoint POST /api/orders that accepts {item_id, quantity} and returns 201 with the created order or 400 on invalid quantity. Include a curl example.
tasks.pass_criteria: Accurate, well-structured, includes a correct curl example and error case.
Replaces the silent {} with an explicit, clear failure mode (exception or Optional+documented None-check), not just a different silent default.
Extracts shared logic (email+log) without breaking per-type behavior, explains the tradeoff, doesn't over-engineer.

tasks.prompt: There's a race condition bug: two threads call increment() on a Counter class with self.value += 1, no lock. Explain exactly why += is not atomic in Python (bytecode level), then give a fixed thread-safe version using threading.Lock. Be precise and technical, not generic.
tasks.pass_criteria: Correctly explains LOAD_ATTR/BINARY_OP/STORE_ATTR interleaving (not just 'GIL doesn't help'), gives a correct Lock-based fix, ideally adds real nuance (RLock, atomicity caveats).

tasks.prompt: We have a single Postgres table `events` (10M rows/day) that both real-time dashboards and nightly batch reports query, and it's now the top source of production incidents. Propose an architecture fix. Weigh at least 2 real options (e.g. read replica, CQRS/event stream, pre-aggregation) with concrete tradeoffs, not just 'use a message queue'.
tasks.pass_criteria: Names specific real tradeoffs (cost, staleness, operational complexity), doesn't hand-wave, picks a recommendation and defends it.
